mainTopic: Mixed intentions in עבודה (רבי יוחנן and אילפא), and whether the first name or thought decides: the תמורה of an עולה and a שלמים, אביי and רבא, and רב דימי's link to רבי יהודה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous page: the רישא of the משנה is about two עבודות, while the סיפא covers one עבודה and two. The words 'זה הכלל' in רבי יהודה's ruling fit רבי יוחנן but are hard to explain for אילפא, and the גמרא leaves this as a קשיא. Then the גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תמורה. There, רבי מאיר says that if someone names one animal 'the תמורה of an עולה, the תמורה of a שלמים', only the first name counts. רבי יוסי says both names count if he planned both from the start. The גמרא asks what happens if both names are said together or if he says he wants to split the animal. אביי says רבי מאיר agrees in that case, and רבא says they still argue. רבא challenges אביי from שחיטה, and the גמרא adds challenges from קמיצה and the מנחת חוטא. Each time, אביי's side answers that the act can be divided into parts: two סימנים, the קומץ and the לבונה, or the steps of walking to the מזבח. The גמרא reports that some teachers followed אביי and others followed רבא. Finally רב דימי says רבי מאיר is following רבי יהודה's rule 'תפוס לשון ראשון', and he proves it from the משנה about פיגול.

steps.title: The first clause is about two rites, the last clause is about both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers 'yes': the רישא of the משנה can be about two עבודות, while the סיפא, where רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue, covers both one עבודה and two עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. The first part of the משנה is talking about two rites. The last part is talking about one rite and also about two rites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question from the previous page. It says it is fine to read the two parts of the משנה as covering different ranges of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone asked whether the משנה can really be read this way. The answer is yes: the רישא is limited to two עבודות, but the סיפא is broader and includes even a single עבודה. This reading fits רבי יוחנן, who holds the מחלוקת applies even within one עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
A sacrificial rite, such as שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה or זריקה
Yes

phrases.english: Yes; the first clause is about two rites,
phrases.notes: This 'yes' answers a question asked at the end of the previous page.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא – בֵּין בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת בֵּין בִּשְׁתֵּי עֲבוֹדוֹת.
phrases.english: the last clause is about both one rite and two rites.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to a question raised on the previous page about how to divide the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the clauses: each clause of the משנה covers a different range of cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think both clauses must cover the same kinds of cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about two עבודות only. The סיפא covers one עבודה and two עבודות.

steps.title: The words 'this is the general rule' fit רבי יוחנן but not אילפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's 'זה הכלל'. A general-rule phrase suggests a wide principle. That fits רבי יוחנן, but it is unclear what it adds for אילפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה said, this is the general rule: if the thought about time came before the thought about place, the offering is פיגול and one is liable to כרת for it. This makes sense for רבי יוחנן; that is why it says 'this is the general rule.' But for אילפא, what does 'this is the general rule' add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the words of the משנה to challenge אילפא. It argues that the phrase 'זה הכלל' points to a broad rule that also covers a single עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זה הכלל' usually comes to include more cases. For רבי יוחנן it includes the case of one עבודה, where both thoughts happen in the same rite. אילפא limits the מחלוקת to two עבודות, so for him the phrase seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule; usually comes to include more cases
Intending to eat or burn the offering after its permitted time
Intending to eat or burn the offering outside its permitted place
An offering ruined by a wrong thought about time; eating it carries כרת
It makes sense for (one opinion), but...

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Yehuda said, this is the general rule:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמַן קָדְמָה לְמַחְשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם –
phrases.english: if the thought about time came before the thought about place,
it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.
This makes sense according to Rabbi Yochanan;
that is why it teaches 'this is the general rule.'
phrases.notes: For רבי יוחנן, the general rule reaches even the case of one rite.

phrases.english: But according to Ilfa, what does 'this is the general rule' come to add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defending the reading of the משנה to attacking אילפא from רבי יהודה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: אילפא's view that the מחלוקת applies only to two עבודות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'זה הכלל' suggests a broad principle that includes more cases. Under אילפא's narrow view, no extra case is left for it to include.

steps.title: The challenge against אילפא stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes with 'קשיא': the question on אילפא stays unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for אילפא here. The question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the challenge has not been answered. It is weaker than a full rejection of the view, but the wording of the משנה clearly fits רבי יוחנן better.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: 'זה הכלל' in רבי יהודה's words supports רבי יוחנן, who says the מחלוקת applies even within one עבודה. Against אילפא it stays a קשיא.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 2 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question on אילפא is not answered; the משנה's wording fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: A משנה in תמורה: one animal named for both an עולה and a שלמים
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תמורה. A person says about one animal, 'this is the תמורה of an עולה, the תמורה of a שלמים.' רבי מאיר rules it is the תמורה of the עולה only.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: if someone says 'this is the substitute of a burnt offering, the substitute of a peace offering,' it is the substitute of the burnt offering. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This sets up a question about two names given to one animal, one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one person gives one animal two different holy names. רבי מאיר says only the first name, עולה, takes effect. This is like the earlier topic of two thoughts during a קרבן, where the first one may decide the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal substituted for a קרבן; it becomes holy too
A burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח
A peace offering, mostly eaten by the owners

steps.whyThisMatters: It opens the question of whether the first name or thought always wins when two come one after the other. This ties back to רבי יהודה's view about which thought came first.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת תמורה.

phrases.english: 'This is the substitute of a burnt offering, the substitute of a peace offering' —
it is the substitute of the burnt offering.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the קשיא on אילפא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: when one animal is named the תמורה of an עולה and then of a שלמים, only the first name, עולה, takes effect.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: it depends on what he planned from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if the person planned both names from the start, both names count, since no one can say two names at the same instant. If he only changed his mind after saying 'עולה', it is an עולה alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: if he meant this from the start, then since it is impossible to say two names at once, his words stand. But if after he said 'this is the substitute of a burnt offering,' he changed his mind and said 'this is the substitute of a peace offering,' it is a burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי argues with רבי מאיר and divides the case in two. What matters is whether the person planned both names before he began speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's reasoning: a person cannot say two words in the same moment, so if he planned both names together, saying them in order does not mean the first one wins. If he only thought of the second name after saying the first, the first name has already taken effect and the second does nothing. This is the 'one thing after another' question the גמרא will compare to the topic of intentions.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it from the start

keyTerms.term: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהוֹצִיא שְׁתֵּי שֵׁמוֹת כְּאַחַת
keyTerms.meaning: It is impossible to say two names at the same instant
His words stand; what he said takes effect
He changed his mind

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not disagree that the second name fails if the person only changed his mind afterward. He disagrees only when both names were planned from the start.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
If this is what he intended from the start,

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהוֹצִיא שְׁתֵּי שֵׁמוֹת כְּאַחַת –
phrases.english: since it is impossible to say two names at once,
his words stand;
but if after he said 'this is the substitute of a burnt offering,'
he changed his mind and said 'this is the substitute of a peace offering,'
it is a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: if both names were planned from the start, both take effect. If the second name came only from a change of mind, only the first name, עולה, counts.

steps.title: Two new questions about naming both offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the law is if someone says 'תמורת עולה ושלמים' in one phrase, and what the law is if he says he wants to split the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if a person says, 'This is the תמורה of an עולה and a שלמים,' what is the law? And if he says he means 'to split' it between them, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks two follow-up questions on the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי from the previous step. This sets up the answers of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the person said 'תמורת עולה, תמורת שלמים', which sounds like two separate sayings. Here the wording ties the two names together, either by joining them with 'and' or by saying clearly that he wants to split the animal. The question is whether רבי מאיר would still say only the first name counts.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים (an open question)
What is the law?
To split it in half, half one offering and half the other

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
"This is the substitute of an עולה and שלמים", what is the law?
"To split", what is the law?
phrases.notes: He says outright that he wants the animal to be half עולה and half שלמים, even though he still says עולה first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argument to new wordings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי מאיר still say only the first name counts when the two names are joined, or when splitting is stated clearly?

steps.title: אביי: here רבי מאיר agrees
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that in this case רבי מאיר surely agrees that both names count.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In this case רבי מאיר certainly agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the questions of step 6. In these cases, where the two names are joined or a split is stated outright, even רבי מאיר agrees that both offerings take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר only follows the first word when the person might have changed his mind partway through. When the person says clearly that he wants to split the animal, there is no change of mind, so both names count.

keyTerms.meaning: In this case
Certainly
Agrees, admits

phrases.english: אביי said:
In this case רבי מאיר certainly agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי בהא ודאי מודה רבי מאיר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When splitting is stated clearly, רבי מאיר agrees that both offerings take effect.

steps.title: רבא: they still argue
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with אביי and says רבי מאיר still argues even in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is still a disagreement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite answer: even here, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי still argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, רבי מאיר follows the first name said in every case. Saying 'to split' does not help, because the word עולה still came first and took hold right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Still
A disagreement

phrases.english: רבא said:
It is still a disagreement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even when splitting is stated clearly, רבי מאיר holds that only the first name counts.

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי from our משנה about שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that a שחיטה with two thoughts is like 'splitting', and yet רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about it in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: According to you, who says that in this case רבי מאיר certainly agrees, look at שחיטה. It is like 'splitting', and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's view. He uses our משנה, where a person slaughters with one thought about time and another about place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering is one act, so both thoughts are held during that one act. That looks like 'splitting' the animal between the two thoughts. Still, in our משנה רבי יהודה follows the first thought, so the split does not make him agree. That goes against אביי's idea that a clear split ends the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you
Slaughtering the animal
Is like, is comparable
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: Our משנה is an argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים, not רבי מאיר. רבא is comparing the two arguments, since both are about whether the first thing said wins.

phrases.english: רבא said to אביי:
According to you, who said
that in this case רבי מאיר certainly agrees;
look at slaughtering,
phrases.notes: This refers to our משנה: he slaughters meaning to eat a כזית past its time and a כזית outside its place.

phrases.english: which is like "to split",
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and yet they argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבא לאביי לדידך דאמרת בהא ודאי מודה רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that a clear split makes even the 'first name counts' view agree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שחיטה with two thoughts is a split within one act, yet our משנה records an argument. So a split does not end the argument.

steps.title: אביי: שחיטה happens step by step
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that שחיטה is a process from start to finish. Our משנה is about one thought on the first סימן and a different thought on the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do you think שחיטה only counts at the very end? No, שחיטה happens from the beginning to the end. Our משנה is about a person who said: the first סימן past its time, the second סימן outside its place.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his view. He shows that our משנה is not a 'split' case at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed שחיטה happens in one instant at the end, so both thoughts would be held at the same time. אביי says שחיטה happens step by step, and the person can have one thought while cutting the first סימן and another while cutting the second. That is like two separate sayings, so the argument there fits fine with אביי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: At the end
From beginning to end
One of the two pipes cut in שחיטה, the windpipe or the food pipe
Past its time, meaning a plan to eat it after its allowed time
Outside its place, meaning a plan to eat it outside the allowed area

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: a clear 'split' makes רבי מאיר agree. Our משנה still has an argument because שחיטה happens step by step, so each סימן can carry its own separate thought.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that שחיטה is a process, not one instant, explains how two thoughts during one שחיטה can count as two separate statements.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ אֵינָהּ לִשְׁחִיטָה אֶלָּא לְבַסּוֹף?!
phrases.english: Do you think slaughtering only counts at the end?!
Slaughtering happens from beginning to end;
and our משנה is where he said:
the first סימן is past its time,
the second סימן is outside its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה מי סברת אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: our משנה has two separate thoughts on two סימנים, not a split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שחיטה happens in one instant at the end, so both thoughts are held together, like a split.
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה happens from start to finish, so a thought on each סימן is like a separate statement, and the argument there does not go against אביי.

steps.title: Challenge from taking a handful of a meal offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to קמיצה with two thoughts. It looks like one single act, like 'splitting', and yet רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about קמיצה (taking a handful from a meal offering)? It is like saying 'to split,' and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case to attack אביי. When a כהן takes the handful of a מנחה while thinking two wrong thoughts, that is one act, yet רבי יהודה and the חכמים still argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that when both thoughts are packed into one act ('to split'), everyone agrees both thoughts count, and the argument is only when each thought sits on a different part. קמיצה seems to be one quick act with no parts. So if they argue about it, it seems they argue even in a 'splitting' case, which supports רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking a handful of flour out of a meal offering, the key service act of a מנחה
'To split': one thought that covers the offering half one way and half the other
They disagree

phrases.english: But there is the taking of the handful,
phrases.notes: He means a כהן who took the handful while thinking of eating it beyond its time and also outside its place.

phrases.english: which is like 'to split,' and yet they disagree!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'which is like.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי קְמִיצָה דִּכִי לַחֲצוֹת דָּמֵי וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי answered the שחיטה challenge by splitting it into two סימנים, the גמרא brings a new case that seems to have no parts.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר and everyone agree both names count when the two thoughts are said together in one act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קמיצה is a single act like 'splitting,' yet רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about it, so the argument exists even in a 'splitting' case.

steps.title: The argument is about burning two separate items
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case in the argument is really about burning the קומץ with one thought and the לבונה with another thought. Those are two separate acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where he burned the handful of the meal offering with a thought of 'beyond its time,' and the handful of frankincense with a thought of 'outside its place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by reading the argument about the מנחה differently. The argument is not about one act of קמיצה. It is about the burning of two different items, each with its own thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה has two items that are burned on the מזבח: the handful of flour (קומץ) and the frankincense (לבונה). If one thought was on the קומץ and a different thought on the לבונה, there are two parts with two thoughts. That is exactly the kind of case where אביי said they argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Burned on the מזבח
The handful of flour taken from the מנחה
Frankincense that is burned together with many meal offerings
A thought to eat or offer it after its allowed time
A thought to eat or offer it outside its allowed place

phrases.english: There too,
phrases.notes: Just like the שחיטה answer in step 10, this case can also be split into two parts.

phrases.english: it is where he burned the handful of the meal offering with a thought of 'beyond its time,'
and the handful of frankincense with a thought of 'outside its place.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי שֶׁהִקְטִיר קוֹמֶץ מִנְחָה חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קמיצה challenge in the same way step 10 answered the שחיטה challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא): the argument is about two separate acts, not one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument about the מנחה is about one act of קמיצה with two thoughts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about burning the קומץ and the לבונה, two items with two separate thoughts.

steps.title: Challenge from the sinner's meal offering, which has no frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. A מנחת חוטא has no לבונה, so there is only one item to burn, and still they argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the handful of a sinner's meal offering? It has no frankincense with it, and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the last answer. In a sinner's meal offering there is no frankincense, so the trick of 'one thought on the קומץ, one on the לבונה' cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer needed two items to hold two thoughts. A מנחת חוטא has only the קומץ, so it looks like one act with both thoughts. If they still argue about it, רבא's view seems right again.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner's meal offering, brought by a very poor person for certain sins; it has no oil or frankincense
That there is not
With it

phrases.english: But there is the handful of a sinner's meal offering,
which has no frankincense with it, and yet they disagree!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי קוֹמֶץ דְּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא דְּלֵיכָּא לְבוֹנָה בַּהֲדֵיהּ וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 by bringing a מנחה that has only one item to burn.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the argument is about the קומץ and the לבונה as two separate parts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without לבונה there is only one item, so the case cannot be split, yet they argue.

steps.title: First answer: there is no argument there
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: in the case of a מנחת חוטא, רבי יהודה and the חכמים do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply denies that there is an argument about the sinner's meal offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no argument exists in this one-item case, it fits אביי perfectly. In a single act with both thoughts, everyone agrees that both thoughts count.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not disagree

phrases.english: They do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the מנחת חוטא by denying the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise: there is no argument in that case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue even about the one-item מנחת חוטא.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the מנחת חוטא they agree, which fits אביי.

steps.title: רב אשי: if they argue, it is about the steps of walking
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives another answer. Even if they do argue about a מנחת חוטא, the argument is about different thoughts during the different steps of carrying the קומץ to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even if you say they disagree, they disagree about the steps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to defend אביי. Even a single קומץ can be divided into parts, because carrying it to the מזבח takes several steps, and each step can have its own thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking the קומץ to the מזבח is a service act, and it is made of many steps. If the כהן had one thought on some steps and another thought on later steps, that is two parts with two thoughts. So even this case fits אביי's rule that the argument is only when the thoughts sit on different parts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you want to say,' meaning: even if we accept your claim
Steps, the paces taken while carrying the קומץ to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's position holds all the way through. Wherever רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue, the two thoughts can be placed on different parts of the service: two סימנים, the קומץ and the לבונה, or separate steps of walking. When both thoughts are in one single act ('to split'), everyone agrees both count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא can break almost any service act into smaller parts. That saves אביי's distinction between 'one act with both thoughts' and 'separate thoughts on separate parts.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even if you say that they disagree,
they disagree about the steps.
phrases.notes: These are the steps the כהן takes carrying the handful to the מזבח, thinking one thing on some steps and another thing on others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר פְּלִיגִי פְּלִיגִי בִּפְסִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of step 13, for someone who does not accept that there is no argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case (אוקימתא): splitting the act of carrying into separate steps
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single קומץ with no לבונה must be one act with both thoughts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a single קומץ is carried in several steps, so the thoughts can sit on different parts.

steps.title: Two teachers pass down the teaching in two different ways
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי taught the teaching like אביי, and רב הונא בר נתן taught it like רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי used to teach this like אביי. רב הונא בר נתן used to teach it like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument between אביי and רבא without picking a winner. It simply reports that some teachers followed אביי's version and others followed רבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי held that when someone says both things at the very same moment, even רבי מאיר agrees both take effect. רבא held that even then, רבי מאיר counts only the first. After all the challenges and answers, both views still stand, and this line tells us each one had its own line of teachers.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to teach (this teaching in a certain way)
Like / in line with

steps.whatToRemember: The אביי and רבא argument is left open. Each side had teachers who passed it down their way.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי כִּדְאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi would teach it like Abaye,

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר נָתָן מַתְנֵי כִּדְרָבָא.
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Natan would teach it like Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי כִּדְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge-and-answer cycle about אביי's view by recording that both versions were taught.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no final decision between אביי and רבא. Each view has its own line of teachers.

steps.title: רב דימי: רבי מאיר is following רבי יהודה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי says רבי מאיר's ruling comes from רבי יהודה's general rule that we go by the first statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי מאיר said his ruling based on the view of רבי יהודה, who says, 'Hold onto the first statement.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רב דימי, arrives from ארץ ישראל and gives a fresh explanation of רבי מאיר's ruling. He links it to a rule of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רבי מאיר's ruling looked like his own idea about how two statements in a row work. רב דימי says it is not unique to רבי מאיר. It is really רבי יהודה's wider rule that the first thing said is what counts. This opens a new line of discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: When (a teacher) came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Following the approach/view of
Hold onto the first statement; the first thing said decides

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר – בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said it following the view of Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי מאיר's ruling that 'a substitute for an עולה, a substitute for a שלמים' becomes only a substitute for an עולה.

phrases.english: who says: hold onto the first statement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the אביי and רבא discussion ends, a new explanation of רבי מאיר's ruling is offered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר's ruling is based on רבי יהודה's principle that the first statement decides.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי shows where רבי יהודה says the first statement counts: in the משנה about mixed thoughts of time and place during a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה said, this is the rule: if the thought about time came before the thought about place, the קרבן is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to back up רב דימי's claim that רבי יהודה goes by the first statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought about eating the קרבן too late (time) makes it פיגול, which carries כרת. A thought about eating it in the wrong place only makes it unfit, without כרת. רבי יהודה says that if the time thought came first, it is פיגול, so the first thought decides. That is exactly 'hold onto the first statement.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
A thought to eat or burn the קרבן after its proper time
A thought to eat or burn the קרבן outside its proper place
A קרבן ruined by a wrong-time thought; eating it carries כרת
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two thoughts. Only the time thought makes פיגול with כרת. The place thought makes the קרבן unfit, but without כרת.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל:
phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said, this is the rule:
If the thought about time came first,
before the thought about place,
it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב דימי's claim that רבי יהודה holds 'תפוס לשון ראשון'.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה rules by the first statement or thought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי יהודה rules that if the time thought came before the place thought, the קרבן is פיגול with כרת.
